hypothesis: Pre-survey benthic light availability contains out-of-time information about Thalassia plant condition beyond persistent transect identity, survey context, visit depth and bulk water clarity.

blade_length_mean_mm.direction: not predeclared; low light can alter morphology non-monotonically

shoot_density_mean_m2.direction: not required for predictive endpoint; biological expectation is lower density under chronic light stress

baseline.rationale: Controls persistent site identity, secular/seasonal survey context, effort, depth itself and bulk water clarity before testing the nonlinear light-at-depth proxy.

validation.split: strict walk-forward by target year; training uses only earlier years

interpretation.supported: Benthic-light dose is a candidate dynamic mechanism for plant condition above the information in depth and segment-level Secchi separately.
interpretation.unsupported: This simplified segment-Secchi x visit-depth light proxy does not add robust annual predictive information; finer optical data, epiphytes, event-scale stress or below-ground legacy remain unresolved.

claim_boundary: Post-hoc exploratory mechanism test, not causal identification.
Segment-level Secchi does not provide node-specific optical conditions.
Beer-Lambert exposure omits spectral quality, epiphytes, bottom reflectance and canopy self-shading.
Do not alter the exposure window, outcomes, baseline, estimability rules or support threshold after opening the response result.
The 3-month sensitivity cannot replace an adverse or null 6-month primary result.
